question.text: This battle was a disastrous defeat of Hannibal by the Roman general Scipio Africanus. This battle was so detrimental to Carthage that it resulted in the immediate end of the Second Punic War.
question.clue: The right wing of this battle was composed of cavalry under the direction of Massinissa.

swap.leadin: China wasn't the only country that built great walls.
swap.text: This Roman emperor built a namesake wall to mark the northern boundary of Roman Britain. He also suppressed the Bar Kokhba revolt in Judea.
swap.clue: He twice avoided war with Parthia and he put down Bar Kokhba's Revolt, but he also defified his drowned lover, the Greek youth Antinous.

question.leadin: The Batavian Revolt began during this time period, which started with an assassination led by prefect Nymphidius Sabinus.
question.text: Identify this time period which saw the rule of men like Otho and Vitelleus.
question.answerHtml: Year of the Four Emperors [prompt on “69 AD”]
question.clue: It saw the exile of Cartimandua, queen of the Brigantes, after a revolt by her husband Venutius, as well as two major battles at Bedriacum or Cremona.

swap.text: After Teutoburg Forest, this emperor would periodically bash his head into a wall while yelling "Quinctilius Varus, give me back my legions!" This emperor won the Battle of Actium.
swap.clue: This ruler reportedly shouted at Quintilius Varus to "give me back my legions" after his forces lost the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest.

question.text: Most Roman chariot racing took place at this stadium, where Diocles is estimated to have won over 1200 times. This venue was the largest sporting venue in Ancient Rome and is estimated to have held seating for around 250,000 spectators.
question.clue: This stadium, which predated the Republic of Rome, had a large track that was used for chariot racing, but today only a patch of grassland remains.

swap.text: The Capitoline Hill is at one end of this general area of Rome, where most of the politics of the day took place. The arch of Titus leads into this area, which contains the temple of Diana.
swap.clue: This place replaced the Comitium and was the site of the Basilica Aemilia.The Arch of Titus is located on the Via Sacra southeast of this place that is located between the Palatine and Capitoline Hills.

question.leadin: This woman's revolt occurred after the death of her husband Prasutagus and the rape of her two daughters.
question.text: Name this Iceni queen who revolted against the Roman Empire. She either died from sickness or via suicide after the failure of the revolt.
question.clue: This whip-scarred ruler avenged the rape of two daughters according to the Annals of Tacitus, whose Agricola barely discusses this consort of Prasutagus sacking Camulodunum ("cam-oo-LOH-doo-num") and Londinium.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the rise of Rome.
swap.text: Rome's first king and legendary founder was this man. This man murdered his twin brother, Remus.
swap.clue: Fighting between factions loyal to him and factions loyal to Tatius eventually led to Numa Pompilius being crowned as this man's successor.

question.leadin: Answer the following about people who may have come from Lydia or Umbria.
question.text: This Italian civilization, which was eventually absorbed by the Romans, had no centralized government. Instead, it was comprised of a loose Confederation of cities like Clusium and Veii.
question.clue: The names of gods in this language are on a sheep liver-shaped bronze artifact used for haruspicy found at Piacenza.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Emperor Augustus's religious reforms.
swap.text: Suetonius (sweh-TOH-nee-uss) notes that Augustus revived this February festival, whose celebrants sacrifice goats, then don strips of the goatskin while running a circuit around the Palatine Hill that started and ended in a cave.
swap.clue: This event originated when King Amulius ordered two men to be thrown into the Tiber River as punishment.

question.leadin: This ruler attempted to seek the aid of Lars Porsena, the king of Clusium, after an action committed by his son Sextus.
question.text: Name this ruler. This ruler was overthrown by a group that included his own nephew Lucius Junus Brutus.
question.answerHtml: Lucius Tarquinius Superbus [accept Tarquin the Proud; prompt on Tarquin; do NOT accept or prompt on "Lucius Tarquinius Priscus" or "Tarquin the Elder"]
question.clue: This ruler took refuge with Aristodemus of Cumae after a battle in which Castor and Pollux purportedly fought against him.

swap.leadin: Identify these things related to the early days of Rome.
swap.text: The revolt that resulted in Tarquinius' deposition was sparked by his son's rape of this woman.
swap.clue: After that, a man threatened to place the naked corpse of a slave next to this woman's bed to frame her for adultery.

question.leadin: Decabalus was the last independent leader of this region.
question.text: Name this region that was conquered by Trajan, which he depicted in his column. It had its capital at Sarmizegetusa.
question.clue: Soldiers of this region used the sickle-like falx during a war in which a bridge near the Iron Gates was built by Apollodorus.

swap.text: Hannibal's most effective opponent in Italy was this Roman, who avoided battles and used attrition to weaken Hannibal's army; he now lends his name to such strategies.
swap.answerHtml: Quintus Fabius Maximus Verrucosus [or Fabius Cunctator; accept Fabian strategy]
swap.clue: This Roman leader or his namesake strategy that he employed after the Battle of Lake Trasimene. His strategy involved wearing down an opponent and avoiding frontal assaults and decisive battles, which annoyed the public.

question.leadin: Answer the following about attacks on Roman control in Hispania.
question.text: This former shepherd and leader of the Lusitani rose up against Roman control after a governor dug a trench around a group of Lusitani and killed them while they were surrendering their weapons. This leader defeated a Roman army at the Battle of Mt. Veneris.
question.clue: When Rome first conquered Lusitania, there was an anti-Roman rebellion led by this man. Livy started the tradition that this man was a shepherd, which is how he is portrayed in the Lusiads.

swap.leadin: In a poem describing God, he wrote that God "is indescribable" even to Jesus.
swap.text: Name this author of "Thalia" whose views were criticized by Athanasius (ath-uh-NAY-shus) in On the Councils of Ariminum and Seleucia (uh-RIM-in-um and si-LOO-shuh)
swap.clue: While speaking at an event, this person was apocryphally slapped by an outraged man from Patara.

question.text: This confederate of the lawyer Celestius wrote the tract On Free Will but was condemned by Pope Zosimus at the Council of Carthage for his belief in the ability of men to save themselves.
question.clue: This British heretic, who famously denied original sin and incurred the wrath of St. Augustine.

swap.leadin: Appius Claudius precipitated the first of these events by passing a law that reinforced the right of creditors to imprison their debtors.
swap.text: Identify these events, of which there were at least five in total. The second of them was a protest against the abuses of the decemviri, or the men who implemented the Twelve Tables.
swap.answerHtml: plebeian secessions [or secessions of the plebs; or secessio plebis; accept synonyms for “secession” such as withdrawal; prompt on “secession” or “withdrawal”]

question.leadin: Identify these key figures from the first six books of Tacitus' Annals.
question.text: Name the perfidious governor of Syria and crony of Tiberius suspected of poisoning Germanicus, of whom Tacitus wrote: "he carried corruption to such a pitch that in the language of the rabble he was known as the Father of the Legions."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the phrase "In hoc signo vinces," FTPE.
swap.text: The story of vision of the cross was told by this lackey of Constantine, a historian from Caesarea who described the early years of Christianity in his Ecclesiastical History.
swap.clue: Two advisors to Constantine had this name. The one from Caesarea wrote histories like the Chronicon.
